title: An exact fully faithful left adjoint with zero-kernel right adjoint is an equivalence
statement: Let $\mathcal D$ and $\mathcal D\prime$ be triangulated categories [def-weil-triangulated-category], and let $F:\mathcal D\to\mathcal D\prime$ and $G:\mathcal D\prime\to\mathcal D$ be exact functors. Suppose $F$ is fully faithful (bijections on all morphism sets), there is a specified adjunction $F\dashv G$ (natural Hom-set bijections with unit $\eta$ and counit $\varepsilon$ satisfying the triangle identities), and $G(Y)\simeq0$ implies $Y\simeq0$ for every $Y\in\mathcal D\prime$. Then $F$ and $G$ are inverse equivalences: both $\eta:\operatorname{id}\to GF$ and $\varepsilon:FG\to\operatorname{id}$ are natural isomorphisms.

proof.text: Apply [lem-sp-adjunction-unit-fully-faithful-left] to the specified adjunction $F\dashv G$. Its hypothesis is exactly full faithfulness of $F$, so $\eta:\mathrm{id}_{\mathcal D}\to GF$ is a natural isomorphism.

source.place: Tag 07RB, lemma-adjoint-fully-faithful (1), as invoked in the first sentence of Tag 09J1.

proof.text: Fix $Y\in\mathcal D\prime$. The right triangle identity is $G(\varepsilon_Y)\circ\eta_{GY}=\mathrm{id}_{GY}$. Step 1 makes $\eta_{GY}$ invertible, hence $G(\varepsilon_Y)=\eta_{GY}^{-1}$ is invertible. By TR1 of [def-weil-triangulated-category], choose a distinguished triangle $FGY\xrightarrow{\varepsilon_Y}Y\to C_Y\to(FGY)[1]$. Exactness of $G$, as defined there, gives a distinguished triangle $GFGY\xrightarrow{G(\varepsilon_Y)}GY\to GC_Y\to(GFGY)[1]$, where the last arrow uses the shift comparison of $G$.

Apply [lem-kun-distinguished-cone-zero] in $\mathcal D$ to the image triangle of step 2. Its first map is invertible, so $GC_Y\simeq0$. The zero-kernel hypothesis of the item, applied to $C_Y$, implies $C_Y\simeq0$. Apply the same cited criterion in $\mathcal D\prime$ to the original triangle: its third vertex is zero, so $\varepsilon_Y:FGY\to Y$ is invertible.

The counit is already natural. For $a:Y\to Y\prime$, its naturality equation $a\circ\varepsilon_Y=\varepsilon_{Y\prime}\circ FG(a)$ implies $FG(a)\circ\varepsilon_Y^{-1}=\varepsilon_{Y\prime}^{-1}\circ a$ by composing with the two inverses. Thus the component inverses form a natural inverse to $\varepsilon$. Together with the natural isomorphism $\eta$ from step 1, these give the asserted inverse equivalences $F$ and $G$.
